front_blocks.md: Name the three main fossil fuels.

back_blocks.md: The three main fossil fuels are **coal**, **natural gas** and **petroleum** (also called crude oil).

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Fractions collected from the top of a fractionating column have longer carbon chains and higher boiling points than those collected from the bottom.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Fractions collected from the top have **shorter carbon chains** and **lower boiling points**. Fractions with longer chains and higher boiling points condense near the bottom of the column.

front_blocks.md: State the use of each of these petroleum fractions: refinery gas, gasoline and naphtha.

back_blocks.md: Refinery gas is used for **heating and cooking**. Gasoline (petrol) is used as **fuel for cars**. Naphtha is used as a **chemical feedstock** for making other chemicals.

cards.front_md: State the use of each of these petroleum fractions: refinery gas, gasoline and naphtha.
cards.back_md: Refinery gas is used for **heating and cooking**. Gasoline (petrol) is used as **fuel for cars**. Naphtha is used as a **chemical feedstock** for making other chemicals.

front_blocks.md: State the uses of diesel oil and bitumen as petroleum fractions.

back_blocks.md: Diesel oil (gas oil) is used as **fuel for diesel engines**. Bitumen is used for **surfacing roads**.

front_blocks.md: Why do longer-chain hydrocarbons condense lower in the fractionating column than shorter-chain hydrocarbons?

back_blocks.md: Longer-chain hydrocarbons have **stronger intermolecular forces**, so they require more energy to remain as vapour and have **higher boiling points**. They condense at the hotter, lower section of the column before shorter-chain hydrocarbons do.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Alkanes are generally unreactive compounds, except that they undergo combustion.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Alkanes contain only strong single covalent bonds, making them generally unreactive. Their main chemical reaction is **combustion** with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water.

front_blocks.md: State the names and molecular formulae of the first four alkanes in order.

front_blocks.md: Why are alkanes generally unreactive compared to alkenes?

back_blocks.md: Alkanes contain only **single carbon-carbon covalent bonds**, which are strong and do not readily break under normal conditions. Alkenes contain a carbon-carbon **double bond**, which is more reactive and allows addition reactions to occur.

front_blocks.md: What is an alkene?

back_blocks.md: An **alkene** is an **unsaturated hydrocarbon** whose molecules contain at least one **carbon-carbon double covalent bond** (C=C).

front_blocks.md: Why are alkenes more reactive than alkanes?

back_blocks.md: Alkenes are more reactive than alkanes because the **C=C double bond** can open up, allowing new bonds to form more easily than the strong single covalent bonds in alkanes.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
An alkane will decolourise aqueous bromine in the same way as an alkene.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
An alkane does not decolourise aqueous bromine and the solution remains orange. Only alkenes, which contain a C=C double bond, react with bromine and decolourise it.

front_blocks.md: Why is cracking economically important?
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: Cracking is economically important because it converts the excess **long-chain hydrocarbons** from **fractional distillation** into more useful shorter-chain fuels (such as **petrol**) and **alkenes** needed for **polymer** production.

front_blocks.md: What is an addition reaction?

back_blocks.md: An addition reaction is one in which atoms from a small molecule add across the **C=C double bond** of an alkene, breaking the double bond and forming **only one product**.

front_blocks.md: Why is only one product formed in an addition reaction?

back_blocks.md: Only one product is formed in an addition reaction because both atoms of the added molecule join across the C=C double bond, leaving no atoms unused and producing a single **saturated compound**.

front_blocks.md: What distinguishes complete combustion of ethanol from incomplete combustion?

back_blocks.md: Complete combustion of ethanol occurs in excess oxygen, producing only **carbon dioxide** and **water**.
Incomplete combustion would occur in limited oxygen and produce **carbon monoxide** or **carbon (soot)** as well.
